target_customer: Engineering teams that send or receive webhooks (SaaS and fintech developers)
problem: Reliably sending and receiving webhooks needs retries, rate limiting, secret rotation and monitoring that each team ends up rebuilding.
business_model: Open-source core with hosted/cloud and enterprise offering (usage or subscription; exact pricing not verified)

founders.name: Subomi Oluwalana
education: Landmark University, Bachelor in Accounting & Finance
founders.background_notes: Backend software engineer who left his job to build fintech APIs.

founders.name: Emmanuel Aina
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in a search summary of funding coverage; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Hookdeck
competitors.traction_then: Launched June 2021; reported doubling users by its April 2022 seed announcement
competitors.funding_then: About $320K pre-seed (closed about September 2021 per BetaKit)

competitors.name: Svix
competitors.what: Webhooks-as-a-service for API providers; also in YC

technical_complexity.rationale: A webhook gateway with retries, rate limiting, circuit breaking and rolling secrets is standard distributed-systems engineering, achievable by a small team but with reliability hard parts at scale.

defensibility.rationale: Open source lowers lock-in and funded competitors (Hookdeck, Svix) were building the same wedge in 2021; integration into a customer's delivery path creates some switching cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence found of incumbents copying or buying Convoy; YC profile still lists it Active. Stripe is mentioned only as the quality benchmark in the company description.

market_need_then: The company says engineering teams struggle to run Stripe-like webhook infrastructure, and at least two other startups raised money in 2021 for the same problem, indicating developer demand and investor interest.
outcome_analysis: Convoy (operated by Frain Technologies, Lagos/London) raised a reported $473K pre-seed in January 2022, around its YC Winter 2022 batch, and remains listed Active with 8 people. It competed with better-funded webhook startups Hookdeck and Svix, the latter of which later raised from a16z; no later round, exit or shutdown for Convoy was found, so its trajectory is unresolved from available sources.
notes: Round figures are from search summaries; the Disrupt Africa page redirected and was not read directly, and the Convoy blog post URL returned 404. Crunchbase-style profiles list $437K; another source claims $970K total including a later $500K convertible note (undated, unverified, not recorded as a round). Founding year varies (2017 vs 2021); YC says 2021.
